mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces the discount rate for equity valuation, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as lower interest rates increase the present value of future cash flows.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS declines over the prior 3 months, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A CPI reading above 200.0 (1982-1984=100) indicates accelerating inflation, triggering a hawkish monetary policy response that increases interest rate expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 200.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.0% and CPI exceeds 195.0, it indicates a tightening monetary policy cycle amid persistent inflation, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as higher interest rates compress equity valuations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where FEDFUNDS > 4.0 AND CPIAUCSL > 195.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Low housing starts (HOUST < 2000.0) indicate weak residential demand, which often precedes a broader economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as equity valuations contract due to reduced growth expectations.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where HOUST < 2000.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates a deteriorating labor market, which often precedes a recession and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as economic growth slows and corporate earnings decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE is rising, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: An unemployment rate above 5.0% signals a deteriorating labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 days as investors react to worsening economic conditions and reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5-day returns in > 60% of instances where UNRATE > 5.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 105.0 and housing starts (HOUST) fall below 2100.0, it indicates a simultaneous slowdown in manufacturing supply and residential demand, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days as the economy enters a contraction phase.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 105.0 AND HOUST < 2100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 100.0) indicates a contraction in manufacturing output, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days as the economy slows and corporate earnings are pressured by reduced demand.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where INDPRO < 100.0, or the Rank IC over a 3-year rolling window is below 0.03.
